name: Koyeb Sandboxes

modes.label: Eco instances (2 GB/vCPU, older Milan CPUs, was/fra/sin)
modes.note: Same $/h ladder as standard but double RAM per vCPU. Eco = AMD EPYC Milan ("half the cores" of the same-priced standard type), max 20 GB disk, no volumes, only in Washington D.C./Frankfurt/Singapore. Offered on Starter/Pro/Scale (instance catalog require_plan). Whether sandboxes may use eco types is not documented. Per second while running. Eco does NOT support Scale-to-Zero at all (docs: Scale-to-Zero needs a Standard CPU or GPU Instance; catalog light_sleep_enabled=false): an eco sandbox never sleeps, so it bills at the full rate until it is deleted (delete_after_delay min 60 s; delete_after_inactivity_delay depends on scale-to-zero and so does not apply). The SDK default sandbox (idle_timeout=300 -> min scale 0) assumes scale-to-zero, so eco sandboxes may be rejected or need idle_timeout=0 (always on).

modes.label: Standard instances (1 GB/vCPU up to 2xlarge, Genoa, all regions)
modes.note: 4 vCPU/8 GiB needs xlarge (8 vCPU/8 GB, $0.1152/h). Local NVMe disk included. The docs say CPU is 'at least 0.25 dedicated vCPU per GB memory, burstable to all cores'. Regions fra, was, sin, tyo, par, sfo (preview); AWS regions on Scale.

modes.label: GPU instances (bundled vCPU/RAM/disk per GPU)
modes.note: GPU instance price includes the bundled vCPU/RAM/disk (e.g. H100 = 15 vCPU/180 GB/320 GB), so vCPU/RAM are 0 here. Regions per the pricing-page instance catalog (2026-09-28): RTX-4000-SFF-ADA in fra/eu only; all other available GPUs in "na" (North America) only. L4 ($0.70) and B200 ($5.50) and 4x H200 / all 8x GPU types are listed but status RESTRICTED with no regions (request access), so L4/B200 are left out of the priced map. Multi-GPU is linear (2x/4x H100 $5/$10). GPU concurrency: Pro 20, Scale 40.

modes.label: Savings plan / long-term reservation (up to 50% off, best case)
modes.commit_note: Pricing page: 'Long-term reservations get up to 50% off the on-demand price.' Term, minimum and the actual discount are negotiated; 0.5 is the published best case.
modes.note: Best-case reading of 'up to 50% off'; sales-only. Verified 2026-09-28: sizes/rates equal the on-demand catalogue (eco-xlarge $0.0576/h, eco-2xlarge $0.1152/h, xlarge $0.1152/h ... https://www.koyeb.com/docs/reference/instances) x 0.5, so eco-xlarge on the plan costs the same as on-demand eco-large by construction, not a data error.

plans.name: Starter (legacy pay-as-you-go)
plans.note: Closed to new signups around 2026-02-26 after the Mistral AI acquisition; existing accounts keep it. Light Sleep fixed at 5 min, deep sleep max 1 h 05.

plans.name: Pro
plans.note: $29/mo with $10 included compute. 10 users, 100 services (each sandbox is a service), 'CPU concurrency 100' (unit ambiguous: instances or vCPU), GPU concurrency 20, 1 TB bandwidth, 7 regions.

plans.name: Scale
plans.note: $299/mo with $100 included compute. 50 users, 1,000 services, CPU concurrency 1,000, GPU 40, AWS regions, 99.9% SLA.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: 'Starting at $1000/mo' with $500 included usage (comparison table). Custom CPU/RAM/GPU, 50 regions, BYOC, dedicated racks, SSO/RBAC/audit, ISO27001/SOC2, 99.99% SLA.

extras.item: Custom domains beyond included (100 Pro / 500 Scale)

perf_source: No benchmark row: provider is not in ComputeSDK results or the HPC run (as of 2026-09-28). See research/perf-map.json.

knobs.label: Idle period before scale-to-zero (x session hours)
knobs.why: Between the last request and the idle period expiring the instance bills its full rate; the minimum idle period is 5 min on all plans (Light Sleep windows 5 min-3 h Pro / 6 h Scale). Deep sleep is $0 and Light Sleep is free only during preview. Factor = (session + idle period) / session, e.g. 5 min on 30-min sessions = 1.17x.

caveats: Plan fees are only partly usage credit: Pro $29 includes $10, Scale $299 includes $100, Enterprise from $1,000 includes $500. Starter (no fee) is closed to new signups since about 2026-02-26 (flag legacy).
Eco eligibility for sandboxes is undocumented. Eco-xlarge fits 4/8 exactly at $0.0576/h; standard needs xlarge 8/8 at $0.1152/h. Eco = older Milan CPUs, 20 GB disk max, no volumes, was/fra/sin only.

Light Sleep (~200 ms wake) is free only during public preview; a GA price is announced but unpublished. Deep sleep and paused services are $0. The idle period before sleeping (min 5 min) is billed at the full rate.
'CPU concurrency' 100 (Pro) / 1,000 (Scale) may count vCPUs rather than instances; if vCPUs, 50 x 4-vCPU sandboxes require Scale.

Sandbox snapshots (FILESYSTEM, or FULL with running processes) and spawn-from-snapshot exist only in the official SDK (koyeb-sdk >= 1.5.2, 2026-08-27, labelled experimental); not documented on koyeb.com and no snapshot price published (snapshot_gib_month null). Volumes (preview, 1-10 GB, was/fra, standard/GPU only, not eco) and volume snapshots were 'free during the public preview' (blog); an unverified search snippet cites 10 GB free then $0.08/GB-month.
Bandwidth: pricing page = 1 TB/mo included on Pro/Scale then $0.02/GB US/EU, $0.04/GB Asia; the older FAQ says 100 GB free then $0.04/GB. Engine uses the pricing page.
features.max_session_h set null (the features file's 24 h is the optional auto-delete maximum, not a forced session limit). delete_after_inactivity_delay max 12 h after scale-to-zero.
Savings-plan mode uses the published best case (50% off); actual discounts are negotiated.
CPU guarantee is 'at least 0.25 dedicated vCPU per GB memory, burstable to all cores', so a standard 1 GB/vCPU instance may get less than its nominal vCPUs under contention.
Startup program up to $30k credits (not in free).
No benchmark data for Koyeb in benchmarks.json.

Verifier 2026-09-28 (pricing page embedded instance catalog): GPU regions corrected from us/eu/asia to us (na) + eu (RTX-4000-SFF-ADA only); L4 and B200 removed from the priced GPU map because their catalog status is RESTRICTED (no regions); eco instances have light_sleep_enabled=false (deep sleep only). Standard, eco and GPU hourly prices, plan fees/included usage, concurrency and bandwidth re-confirmed.

Data residency (DPA): Customer Data stays in the selected region but may move between datacenters within it; global edge routing is not extra compute regions. Core regions FRA, PAR, SIN, TYO, WAS, aws-us-east-1; SFO preview on paid plans. Eco only FRA/WAS/SIN. Egress: $0.02/GB US/EU, $0.04/GB Asia after 1 TB/month (card egress_gib is the US/EU rate). eco-nano hour = per-second $0.0000006 x 3600 = $0.00216 (display rounds to $0.0022). (patches v10-regional, v5-calculators, 2026-09-28)

Official pages conflict: the live pricing page omits Starter and says Enterprise starts at $1,000/month, while the organization reference (updated May 27, 2026) says Starter is available to all users with a valid payment method and Enterprise has a $700/month committed cost. Keep pricing-page values for ranking, but do not present Starter closure or $1,000 as undisputed.

Aggregate cap: the General FAQ says 'With the Scale plan, you can use up to 1TB of memory and up to 1000 services.' So Scale is also capped at ~1 TB of concurrently running RAM (e.g. 125 x 8 GiB sandboxes), and 'CPU concurrency' 100/1,000 most likely counts vCPUs, not instances (unconfirmed). Large fleets need Enterprise.

Sandbox SDK defaults: instance_type 'micro' (0.5 vCPU/512 MB, $0.0072/h), region 'na', idle_timeout 300 s -> deep sleep after 5 min (min scale 0); Light Sleep for sandboxes is only an '_experimental_enable_light_sleep' flag. idle_timeout=0 means always-on (min scale 1).

Billing clock: 'Paid usage begins when an Instance has been created and the Deployment has a Starting status', so image pull/boot time is billed (boot_overhead_s unknown). Usage 'accounted per second and billing is rounded up to the nearest unit'; no minimum billed duration is documented.

Terms: Fees depend on Authorized Users and Services; exceeding the plan's included users/services is 'charged based on usage' but no per-user/per-service price is published. Starter orgs are limited to 1 member (org doc).

fleet.verification: Credit card, $29 preauthorization (immediately cancelled) plus prorated subscription charge; billing details validated and extra information may be requested.
fleet.tiers: Current Pro: 100 services and CPU concurrency 100, GPU concurrency 20; Scale 1,000 services/CPU concurrency 1,000, GPU concurrency 40; Enterprise custom.
fleet.notes: Default left null because entry-page CPU concurrency units and new-account validation overrides do not establish one universal machine-count quota. New signup selects Pro; Starter downgrade/legacy eligibility language conflicts across existing card and FAQ. Validation usually minutes, sometimes up to 3 business days, not an increase SLA.
